title: Infinitive and gerund
description: Present and past infinitive; present and past gerund; stare + gerundio; what the gerund can and cannot do in Italian.
objectives: Use the infinito presente and infinito passato (aver mangiato, essere partito).
Know which prepositions introduce an infinitive, and that dopo requires the past infinitive.
Form the gerundio presente and passato and use stare + gerundio.
Avoid using the gerund where Italian requires an infinitive (after prepositions, as a subject).

blocks.title: Present and past infinitive
blocks.text: The past infinitive is *avere / essere* + participle: *aver mangiato, essere partito/a/i/e*. It expresses an action completed before the main verb. The final -e of *avere/essere* is often dropped before a consonant (*aver detto, esser stato*); both forms are correct.

items: After modal verbs and verbs like *sapere, preferire, lasciare, fare*: *Voglio partire. Lascia parlare la nonna.*
After prepositions: *prima di partire, invece di studiare, senza parlare, per imparare*.
*dopo* requires the **past** infinitive: *dopo aver mangiato* (not *dopo mangiare* in standard Italian).
As a noun (subject or object): *Leggere è bello. Il mangiare.*
In instructions and signs: *Non fumare. Mescolare bene.*

blocks.title: Pronouns attach to the infinitive
blocks.text: The infinitive loses its -e and the pronoun attaches: *vederlo, dirtelo, alzarsi*. With modals the pronoun may also precede the modal (*lo voglio vedere*).

blocks.title: Formation
blocks.text: -are → -ando, -ere/-ire → -endo: *parlando, vedendo, dormendo*. Verbs with an extended imperfetto stem use it: *facendo, dicendo, bevendo*. Gerundio passato: *avendo mangiato, essendo partito/a*.

items: Manner or means: *Ho imparato l'italiano leggendo.* (by reading)
Time: *Tornando a casa, ho visto un gufo.* (while coming home)
Cause: *Essendo stanco, è andato a letto.* (since he was tired)
Condition: *Volendo, potresti finire oggi.* (if you wanted to)
Progressive with *stare*: *Sto leggendo. Stavamo cenando quando è arrivato.*

blocks.title: The gerund's subject
blocks.text: The gerund normally has the same subject as the main verb. *Ho visto Marco uscendo dal negozio* means that *I* was coming out of the shop; to say Marco was, use a relative clause: *Ho visto Marco che usciva dal negozio.*

blocks.title: Not like the English -ing
blocks.text: Italian never uses the gerund after a preposition or as a noun: 'before leaving' = *prima di partire*; 'I like swimming' = *mi piace nuotare*; 'Swimming is healthy' = *Nuotare fa bene*.

blocks.title: stare + gerundio is optional
blocks.text: The simple present already means 'I am doing': *Che cosa fai?* = What are you doing? *stare + gerundio* stresses that the action is in progress right now. It is not used with *essere, avere* or *stare* itself, nor in compound tenses.

examples.it: Dopo aver mangiato, il nonno dormì un'ora.
examples.en: After eating, Grandfather slept for an hour.

examples.it: Prima di uscire, chiudi la finestra.
examples.en: Before going out, close the window.
I learned Italian by reading stories.

examples.it: Stavamo cenando quando è squillato il telefono.
examples.en: We were having dinner when the phone rang.

examples.it: Essendo arrivati tardi, non abbiamo trovato posto.
examples.en: Having arrived late, we didn't find a seat.
examples.note: Gerundio passato with essere: agreement with the subject.

examples.en: Swimming is good for your health.

exercises.explanation: The thing liked is an action: infinitive, with piace (singular).
-ando / -endo; fare, dire, bere use their extended stems (fac-, dic-, bev-).

exercises.prompt: Translate: We were having dinner. (use stare + gerundio)
exercises.explanation: stare in the imperfetto + gerundio. (cenare = to have dinner; also: Stavamo mangiando la cena.)

exercises.prompt: *Ho visto Sara uscendo dal negozio.* Who was coming out of the shop?
exercises.explanation: The gerund's subject is normally the main verb's subject (io). To say Sara was: Ho visto Sara che usciva dal negozio.

exercises.text: Dopo {0} (arrivare, lei), Sara ha telefonato. Dopo {1} (leggere, noi) il libro, abbiamo visto il film.
exercises.explanation: arrivare → essere + agreement (arrivata); leggere → avere. Truncated aver/esser are equally correct.

summary: Infinito passato: avere/essere + participle; dopo + infinito passato.
Infinitive after modals and prepositions, as a noun, in instructions.
Gerundio: -ando/-endo (facendo, dicendo, bevendo); passato: avendo/essendo + participle.
The gerund shares the main subject; never after prepositions; stare + gerundio for actions in progress.

title: The participle
description: The past participle as verb, adjective and participial clause; the present participle.
objectives: Recognise the past participle in compound tenses, the passive and as an adjective.
Understand participial clauses (finita la cena, …) and their agreement.
Recognise the present participle (-ante, -ente) and know it is mostly used as a noun or adjective.

items: Adjective: *una porta chiusa, i bambini stanchi e addormentati*.

blocks.title: Participial clauses
blocks.text: A past participle can form a short clause expressing an action completed before the main one: *Finita la cena, uscimmo* (When dinner was over, we went out). With transitive verbs the participle agrees with the noun it refers to (*Finita la cena*, *Letti i giornali*); with intransitive verbs it agrees with the subject (*Arrivata a casa, Sara si riposò*). This construction is mainly written.

blocks.title: Pronouns attach
blocks.text: In participial clauses pronouns attach to the participle: *Salutatolo, se ne andò* (Having said goodbye to him, she left). This is literary.

blocks.title: -ante, -ente
blocks.text: *cantare → cantante, dormire → dormiente, bollire → bollente*. In modern Italian it survives mainly as an adjective or noun: *un cantante* (a singer), *acqua corrente* (running water), *il presidente*. As a real verb form (*le persone abitanti in città*) it belongs to bureaucratic or literary language; use a relative clause instead (*le persone che abitano in città*).

examples.it: Finita la cena, uscimmo in giardino.
examples.en: When dinner was over, we went out into the garden.
examples.note: Participial clause; finita agrees with la cena.

examples.it: Arrivati alla stazione, i ragazzi comprarono i biglietti.
examples.en: Having arrived at the station, the boys bought the tickets.
examples.note: Intransitive verb: agreement with the subject.
Participle as an adjective describing a state.

examples.it: Il cantante ha una bella voce.
examples.en: The singer has a beautiful voice.
examples.note: Present participle used as a noun.

examples.en: Careful: the water is boiling hot!

examples.it: Letta la lettera, la nonna sorrise.
examples.en: Having read the letter, Grandmother smiled.

exercises.prompt: ___ le lettere, la nonna andò alla posta.
exercises.explanation: Transitive participle in a participial clause agrees with the object it refers to: le lettere → scritte.
Intransitive verb: the participle agrees with the subject (Sara).

options: a past participle used as an adjective
exercises.answer: a past participle used as an adjective
exercises.explanation: aprire → aperto/a: here it describes the noun.

exercises.prompt: Match the present participle to its meaning.
exercises.explanation: Present participles now mostly live as nouns and adjectives.

exercises.prompt: Translate: *Finita la lezione, i bambini uscirono.*
exercises.answer: When the lesson was over, the children went out.
accept: After the lesson ended, the children went out.
When the lesson ended, the children went out.
Once the lesson was over, the children went out.
The lesson over, the children went out.
After the lesson was over, the children went out.
exercises.explanation: A participial clause expressing an earlier action; uscirono is passato remoto.

summary: Past participle: compound tenses, passive, adjective, noun, participial clause.
Participial clauses: agreement with the object (transitive) or subject (intransitive).
Present participle (-ante, -ente): mostly nouns and adjectives today.
